title: Rajratan Global Wire Ltd - 517522 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Rajratan targets 15–20% volume growth and a 50,000-ton Thai expansion (~INR100 crore capex), while management calls current 12.7–13% EBITDA margins the floor.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as revenue and earnings growing faster than volumes, driven by higher utilisation in Chennai and Thailand. Consolidated EBITDA was INR45.79 crore in Q2 versus INR41.71 crore in Q1 (about 10% QoQ, 14% YoY as stated on the call), but EBITDA per ton fell about 3% YoY as input costs rose. Management approved a 50,000-ton Thai brownfield expansion (about INR100 crore) and said Chennai will be ramped from about 30,000 to 60,000 tons over time. Steel cord at Pithampur is still in trials, with about INR70 crore of CWIP not yet capitalised.

segments.name: India (Chennai and Pithampur)
segments.commentary: Chennai is at near full utilisation on the first 30,000 tons, with rated capacity now 40,000 tons and a target of 60,000 tons; FY27 Chennai output guided at 37,000 to 38,000 tons. India volume grew about 14% from H1 to H2 per management.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at about 100% of capacity (about 15,000 tons per quarter, actual Q2 production about 14,600 tons); volume growth 22% per management. Premium customers are about 30% to 32% of Thai sales, targeted to reach about 40% in the coming year.

segments.name: Steel cord (Pithampur, conveyor belting)
segments.commentary: In trials; samples to customers expected next month; ISO and BIS certification still pending. Management is not including steel cord revenue in H2 projections; about INR70 crore of CWIP not yet capitalised, expected to be capitalised around end of this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated volume growth of 15% to 20% YoY for at least the next 10 to 15 quarters; FY27 consolidated volume about 160,000 tons.

Thai 50,000-ton capacity expected within about one year (FY28 H2 start per analyst reading); management projects utilisation within about two years; capex about INR100 crore, funded by internal accruals plus bank loans below 4%.
Chennai to reach 60,000 tons; no firm board approval for any capacity beyond that. Management expects Chennai expansion within about two years if returns justify it.
Management says Thai EBITDA will improve in the coming quarter; little EBITDA improvement expected in India for the remaining two quarters.
Steel price increases expected to continue until mid-November; price hikes to be passed on to remaining customers from December onward.
capex_capacity: Chennai: 30,000-ton first phase nearly fully utilised; rated capacity now 40,000 tons with machines added modularly; monthly output rising from 3,500 to 4,000 tons, then 4,500 tons; 60,000-ton target. Prior capex about INR270 crore for 30,000 tons plus INR30 to 35 crore to complete to 60,000 tons.

Thailand: 50,000-ton brownfield expansion, about INR100 crore (INR125 crore including about INR20 crore for an adjacent factory purchase); expected to be running in about one year, with H2 FY28 start per analyst reading.

Pithampur steel cord: about 10,000 tons planned, with in-house lines still to be installed; a new shed of about 2.5 lakh sq ft has been built; capitalisation expected at end of the quarter after trials.
Pithampur bead wire capacity 72,000 tons total, of which 60,000 tons bead wire (per analyst citing presentation; management confirmed).
Management expects India capacity to reach about 142,000 tons including steel cord once complete (per management correction).
demand_pricing: Indian tyre market growing 8% to 10%; no production cuts by tyre customers in the last year (per management).

India export volume target about 14,000 to 15,000 tons this year, roughly 40% growth; drivers are China-plus-one demand and Rajratan being the only Indian exporter; US subsidiary exists and a Europe subsidiary is planned.
Thailand price gap between premium and Chinese customers can reach THB10,000 per ton (about INR25,000 to 26,000).
Working capital: Europe about 70 to 80 days (including about 40 days transit), US about 90 days, local Thailand about 40 days.
Tariffs: US Section 232 duty of 50% on Indian and Thai steel products; China faces an additional 12.5%.

Competition: management named Tata Steel as the bigger rival and Bansal Wire as a newer entrant. Management said pricing should improve in one to two quarters, and it chose to hold share rather than chase low-price customers.

qa_highlights.question: Thai capacity expansion timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one year to build and two years to fill, with capex of about INR100 crore (INR125 crore including the factory purchase), versus about INR300 crore for a greenfield plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA per ton is down while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input costs (gas, power, diesel, packing, freight) rose sharply; it kept EBITDA per ton roughly stable and does not expect operating leverage to show in the numbers; it sees current margins as the floor.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume and revenue growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15% to 20% volume growth YoY for the next 10 to 15 quarters, with consolidated FY27 volume near 160,000 tons; revenue depends on price.

qa_highlights.question: Green bead wire and Thai export advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Thai feedstock is 92% to 95% scrap-based green steel, which India cannot replicate; this won early approvals with European tyre makers ahead of CBAM. Management declined to forecast the margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: Funding for the Thai capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Combination of internal accruals (Thai balance sheet generating cash monthly) and bank loans below 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Price hikes and margin pressure drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Some hikes taken where prices were not finalised; the rest to be passed on at quarter end. Management said steel prices are rising until mid-November; margin pressure is mainly energy, freight and packing rather than steel.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on price increases; management concedes EBITDA per ton is flat to down YoY and plans to keep competing head-on rather than cutting volume.
Steel cord ramp-up is delayed by certifications (ISO, BIS) and trials; about INR70 crore of CWIP and depreciation and interest will start once capitalised.
Thai utilisation: analyst expects a five to six year fill at 12% to 13% growth; management says about two years, which is a credibility gap to track.
Working capital and borrowings are rising with exports (about 70 to 90 days receivables); consolidated borrowings increased, and the analyst asked for the reconciliation.
Consolidated other income fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited INR3.4 crore to INR0.66 crore); management attributed this to consolidation effects but figures were disputed on the call.
Freight and CBAM volatility under DDP contracts; management is absorbing some risk with freight surcharges.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on volume and Thai growth, but evasive on margins, payback, the steel cord timeline and Chennai beyond 60,000 tons, which management said requires board approval. Several numerical answers were corrected or disputed on the call, so the figures should be checked against filings.
